text: Bitcoin maintains support above $61,500 despite mounting short-term bearish pressure, as digital asset markets brace for macroeconomic tightening. Diminishing expectations for Federal Reserve rate cuts at the upcoming June FOMC meeting—following a surge in May CPI to 4.2%—have bolstered a strong dollar regime. Concurrently, the SEC’s newly unveiled Draft Strategic Plan for FY 2026–2030 signals a strict regulatory posture, reinforcing compliance requirements under evolving frameworks like the EU's MiCA guidelines. This combination of persistent high yields and enforcement focus has cooled retail demand, prompting institutional allocators to pivot search efforts toward stablecoins and yield-bearing tokenized vehicles. The stark divergence highlights a tightening correlation between traditional capital markets and digital assets. As higher-for-longer interest rates strengthen the US Dollar Index, risk-off sentiment directly suppresses cryptocurrency valuations. Traditional liquidity contraction remains the primary transmission channel driving capital outflows from speculative assets into sovereign debt instruments, proving that digital markets are firmly tethered to global macroeconomic policies.
